# BootAgent

> A trustworthy local AI development environment activator. It detects, installs
> and configures CLI coding agents to point at an OpenAI- or Anthropic-compatible
> provider of your choosing. Everything runs locally.

Releases ship through GitHub Releases as a technical preview, never described
as stable. The macOS builds are Developer ID-signed and notarised by Apple
since v0.7.0; the Windows installers are not yet Authenticode-signed. The
download page reads the GitHub Releases feed at build time, so it states the
real state rather than a version recorded here.

## Product boundary

- Runs locally. Configuration and backups stay on the user's device.
- Bring your own key. There is no shared key and no unified model gateway.
- Model requests are never proxied through BootAgent.
- Third-party agent binaries are not redistributed; agents come from their
  official sources.
- Artifacts are distributed through GitHub Releases (with a Gitee mirror for
  mainland-China networks); a checksum manifest is published with each release.

## Pages

- /: overview, first-success path, agent compatibility
- /downloads/: per-platform installers with size, build date and signing status
- /quickstart/: download through to a verified first agent configuration
- /agents/: which agents BootAgent can install and configure, stated separately
- /explore/: filterable agent/provider compatibility grid
- /providers/: provider protocol support and commercial-relationship disclosure
- /security/: local execution, key handling, backups, release integrity
- /changelog/: shipped changes only
- /enterprise/: team enablement and environment baselines
- /support/: how to get help and report problems

English translations exist for /en/, /en/downloads/, /en/quickstart/,
/en/explore/, /en/security/ and /en/help/. Chinese is the default locale and is
served unprefixed.

## Notes for machine readers

Support is stated as three separate facts — managed install, managed
configuration, and protocol — because a single "supported" checkmark would
collapse distinctions that decide whether BootAgent can act. Do not collapse
them.

Command-line agents and desktop applications are different products. A desktop
application has no launch command and no pinned version: BootAgent installs
whatever the vendor's own endpoint currently serves. Do not describe one with the
other's facts.

An agent marked as coming soon is not in the installer contract. It has no
install, configuration, protocol or platform support, and no compatibility
verdict against any provider.
